name: Delhi Sultanate
summary: A series of five Muslim dynasties ruling north India from Delhi. It held off Mongol raids and built the Qutb Minar, until Babur defeated it at Panipat in 1526.

location.value: North India, at times reaching far into the south.

terrain.value: The Indo-Gangetic plain, with campaigns south across the Deccan plateau.

climate.value: Monsoon climate; failed rains caused famine.

resources.value: Fertile farmland, cotton and textiles, and war elephants.

disasters.value: Famine in the 1330s under Muhammad bin Tughluq.

urbanisation.value: Delhi grew into one of the largest cities in the world, with several fortified cities built by different sultans.

migration.value: Turkic, Afghan and Persian elites; refugees fleeing the Mongols.

economicBase.value: Land revenue from farming, collected through iqta (assigned revenue) holders.

tradeRoutes.value: Overland trade with Central Asia and Persia; Indian Ocean trade through Gujarat and Bengal.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: The taka; Muhammad bin Tughluq’s token coinage (1329–1332) failed.

inequality.value: A Turkic, Afghan and Persian Muslim elite ruled over a largely Hindu peasantry.

governmentType.value: Absolute monarchy under a sultan, with five successive dynasties.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Delhi Sultanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate (1999)

keyRulers.value: Qutb ud-Din Aibak, Iltutmish, Razia Sultana (1236–1240), Alauddin Khalji, Muhammad bin Tughluq, Ibrahim Lodi.

succession.value: Often by force; five dynasties (Mamluk, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi).

stability.value: Coups and revolts were common; Timur’s sack (1398) broke central power.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Delhi Sultanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate (1999)

eliteConflict.value: Rival noble factions such as the “Forty” under Iltutmish, and the Khalji Revolution of 1290.
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Delhi Sultanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate (1999)

armyAndTech.value: Heavy cavalry, war elephants and fortified cities; Alauddin Khalji kept a large standing army.

majorWars.value: Repelled Mongol raids; First Battle of Panipat (1526).

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: the Mongols, Rajput kingdoms, Bengal and the Vijayanagara Empire.

inventions.value: The spinning wheel and Persian waterwheel spread in India in this era.

scienceEducation.value: Madrasas and the poet and musician Amir Khusrau.

openness.value: A blend of Persian, Turkic and Indian culture.

religion.value: Sunni Islam as the state religion, ruling a Hindu majority; Jain and other communities.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Delhi Sultanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate (1999)

languageWriting.value: Persian for government; Hindustani developed as a common language.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Delhi Sultanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate (1999)

artsArchitecture.value: The Qutb Minar, Alai Darwaza and Tughlaqabad fort.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Delhi Sultanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate (1999)

socialStructure.value: Sultan, Turkic and Afghan nobles, Hindu chiefs, peasants and slaves.

sharedIdentity.value: Islam and loyalty to the sultan.

neighbours.value: The Mongols, Rajputs, Bengal, the Deccan sultanates and Vijayanagara.

ideasReligions.value: Sufi orders such as the Chishti spread Islam in India.

riseSignals.value: Qutb ud-Din Aibak ruled independently from 1206.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Delhi Sultanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate (1999)

peakPeriod.value: Under the Khaljis and early Tughluqs.

declineSignals.value: Timur’s sack of Delhi (1398) and the rise of regional sultanates.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Delhi Sultanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate (1999)

outcome.value: Babur won at Panipat (1526); succeeded by the Mughal Empire.

sources.value: Persian chronicles. Checked against Wikipedia (“Delhi Sultanate”).

knownFor.label: Razia Sultana
knownFor.note: One of the few women to rule in medieval India.

knownFor.label: Amir Khusrau
knownFor.note: A poet and musician linked to early Hindustani music.
